title: Cut the hot wire to the right length
story: You are building a foam cutter: a piece of 0.4 mm nichrome wire stretched between two posts and heated by a 12 V battery. That wire has 8.75 ohm for every meter. Too short and it pulls so much current that it glows orange and snaps; too long and it never gets hot enough to melt foam. The wire cuts cleanly when the current is between 1 A and 2 A. The four pieces in the box are 0.5 m (4.38 ohm), 1 m (8.75 ohm), 2 m (17.5 ohm) and 4 m (35 ohm). Clip the right piece between the posts.

goals.label: hot-wire current between 1 A and 2 A
almost all of the 12 V lands on the nichrome

hints: Resistance grows in proportion to length: every piece is just 8.75 ohm times its length in meters.
The current is the battery voltage divided by the wire's resistance: try 12 / R for each piece.
